decisions.reason: As a close-to-core supplement line in an expanding large firm with organizational slack and no clear negative signal, management would likely keep it while monitoring whether it reaches aspiration levels.

This skin-and-hair supplement fits the existing consumer-health portfolio, so despite uncertain evidence in a crowded category the firm is likely to retain it unless results clearly fall below aspirations.
The move from a mention to its own page suggests at least acceptable early traction, and because it builds on established capabilities the firm would tend to keep it.
An immune-support supplement matches the firm's portfolio-broadening strategy and appears to have received active launch support, so a slack-rich incumbent would likely continue it.

The documented valsartan problem is a salient performance shortfall for a quality-focused German pharma firm, and behavioral-theory logic suggests management would reallocate resources if confidence stays below aspiration.

Because this OTC migraine product is more distant from the established offer and shows limited evidence of traction beyond launch, management is somewhat more likely to discontinue it and refocus resources.
